name: Circles
intro: **Join the centre to everything.** Radii are free equal lengths, and most circle figures open up once three or four are drawn (§2).
A diameter means a right angle; a tangent with a chord means the alternate segment angle. Mark both on sight (§2, §3).

qs.q: A chord of length 16 cm lies 6 cm from the centre of a circle. Find the radius (in cm).
qs.h: §2 — the perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, giving a right triangle with legs 8 and 6.

qs.q: Two circles of radii 5 and 3 touch externally. The distance between their centres is
qs.h: §6 — external touching means the centre distance is the sum; internal would be the difference.

qs.q: From an external point 13 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 5 cm, find the length of a tangent (in cm).
qs.h: §3, tangents — the tangent is perpendicular to the radius, so use Pythagoras. Look for the 5-12-13 triple.

qs.h: §4, cyclic quadrilaterals — opposite angles are supplementary.

qs.h: The inscribed circle has diameter equal to the side.

audit: grinding through algebra where a Pythagorean triple was staring at you (§2, §3)
using the difference of the radii for externally touching circles — externally means the sum (§6)
forgetting that opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary (§4)
confusing sector with segment, or circumference with area (§1)
taking the square's diagonal as the inscribed circle's diameter — it is the side (§5, §7)
